title: Searching for neural correlates of the hearing sensation fluctuation strength in the auditory cortex of squirrel monkeys.
abstract: Sounds with slow (less than 20 Hz) fluctuations may elicit the hearing sensation fluctuation strength. For AM tones, neural correlates of fluctuation strength were searched in the auditory cortex of unanesthetized squirrel monkeys. To enable a comparison of psychophysical and physiological data, the 'modulation' of the peristimulus time histogram was fitted by a sinusoidal function. The dependence of the amplitude of this function on modulation frequency, modulation depth and sound pressure level was often comparable to the dependence of fluctuation strength on the same stimulus parameters. In particular, as a function of modulation frequency, the neural data also show a bandpass characteristic at low modulation frequencies as was found for the hearing sensation fluctuation strength.
